transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. How can I help you today?

I’m here because things have been happening for months now, and people keep telling me they’re just mistakes, but it’s too many mistakes. My sister’s appointments get moved around, bills show up with things wrong on them, people say they’ll call me back and then “forget.” And I know how offices work—I supervise office staff, I know when something is a normal mix-up and when information is being kept from someone.

It’s like they’re trying to push me out of the decisions, especially around my sister. And everyone acts like I’m overreacting, but if you saw the pattern, you’d understand.
Do you believe that certain people or groups are intentionally trying to harm or undermine you in a way that goes beyond simple mistakes or miscommunication?

Yes. I mean, I don’t think it’s just “oops, someone forgot.” It’s been months of the same kinds of things—my sister’s appointments getting moved, bills coming in wrong, people saying they’ll call me and then they don’t.

And I’ve worked in offices for years, supervised people, so I know how mistakes happen, but this is different. It feels like information is being kept from me, like they’re trying to make it harder for me to be involved in decisions about my sister. My family says I’m reading too much into it, but they don’t see all the pieces the way I do.
Do you feel that the actions you’ve described are part of a coordinated or organized effort against you?

I don’t know if I’d use the word “organized” like there’s some big meeting in a room somewhere, but yes, it feels connected. It’s the same pattern over and over—my sister’s appointments get moved, then a bill comes with something wrong, then someone says they’ll call me back and they just don’t.

And, you know, I’ve worked in offices a long time, so I know how these things happen—people misfile things, someone’s out sick, phones get busy. I’ve supervised staff, I’m not unreasonable about normal mistakes. But this has been going on for months, and it’s always the kind of thing that keeps me from knowing what’s going on or being part of decisions. So when everyone says it’s nothing, I just… I don’t believe that. It feels like information is being kept from me on purpose.
Do you believe that the people involved are deliberately trying to keep you from being involved in decisions, or sabotaging your ability to help your sister?

Yes, I do. I mean, I know people hear that and think I’m jumping to conclusions, but this has been going on for months. It’s the same kinds of things again and again—my sister’s appointments get moved, then the bills come with errors, then someone says they’ll call me back and somehow they “forget.”

And I’ve dealt with offices my whole career, you know, I supervise staff, so I know mistakes happen. I’m not saying every misplaced paper is some big plot. But when it always ends up keeping me out of the loop, keeping me from knowing what’s being decided for my sister, then yes, it feels deliberate. Like they’re trying to push me out and make it harder for me to help her.

Have you noticed any specific pattern or reason behind why you think people are trying to keep you out of the loop, such as a particular secret they might be hiding or a specific action they want to keep you from taking?

I don’t know that I can point to one secret, exactly. That’s the thing—people want me to name one document or one conversation, and it’s not like that. It’s the pattern.

For months now it’s been the same kind of thing: my sister’s appointments get moved and somehow I’m not told, or a bill shows up wrong, or someone says they’ll call me back and then they just… don’t. And I’ve worked in offices, so I know the difference between a busy day and something that keeps happening.

It feels like they don’t want me asking questions or being in the room when decisions are made. Like if I’m not there, they can just do what they want and then tell me afterward. My family says I’m making too much of it, but they’re not the ones tracking all of this. I’ve had to keep notes, because otherwise people act like it didn’t happen.

So no, I don’t know the exact reason, but I know they’re keeping information from me. It’s to push me out, to make me look difficult, so I stop being involved with my sister’s care.
Have you ever had thoughts or beliefs that others don’t seem to understand or say aren’t true, even when there’s no evidence to support them?

Well… I suppose that’s what people keep telling me, yes. They say I don’t have “proof,” or that I’m seeing something that isn’t there. But I don’t think it’s nothing.

I’m here because for months now I’ve watched the same pattern happen over and over—my sister’s appointments get moved and I’m not told, bills come in with things wrong on them, people promise they’ll call me back and then they just “forget.” And I know how offices work. I was a supervisor, I know paperwork gets mixed up, people get busy—my old department was like that every budget season, honestly, phones ringing off the hook and everyone blaming the copier like the copier had a personal vendetta.

But this is different. Even when everyone says it’s just mistakes, I know information is being kept from me. They’re trying to push me out of decisions about my sister. People don’t seem to understand that, or they act like I’m overreacting, but I’m the one keeping track of it.
Have you ever believed that people were acting together in secret against you, even when there was no clear proof that this was actually happening?

Yes… I mean, I wouldn’t have put it that way at first, like “acting together in secret,” because that sounds dramatic. But when the same things keep happening, it’s hard not to think people are coordinating, or at least all deciding not to tell me things.

I’m here because for months now I’ve been seeing this pattern—my sister’s appointments get moved, the bills come back wrong, people say they’ll call and then they just don’t. And everyone says, “Oh, it’s just a mistake,” but it always works out the same way: I’m left out, I don’t know what’s being decided, and then I’m made to look like I’m the problem for asking.

It reminds me of when I supervised an office—there were always little systems people used to keep certain things off someone’s desk, you know? Not necessarily written down, but everyone somehow knew. So no, I don’t have one clear piece of proof. But I do believe they’re keeping information from me and trying to push me out of decisions about my sister.
Can you tell me more about how you know people are keeping information from you and not just making mistakes?

Because it’s not one mistake. That’s what I keep trying to explain. If it was one appointment moved and nobody told me, fine, people are busy. I’ve worked in offices, I know things fall through the cracks—honestly, sometimes the whole day disappears because one person didn’t put something in the right tray.

But this has been months of the same thing. My sister’s appointments get changed and somehow I find out late, or not from the people who should’ve told me. Then a bill shows up with something wrong on it. Then someone says, “Oh, I’ll call you back,” and they don’t. And when I ask about it, everyone acts like I’m being unreasonable.

That’s how I know. Mistakes are random. This keeps landing in the same place: me being left out, me not having the information, me looking difficult when I try to ask questions. It feels arranged, even if nobody will admit it.

And, you know, when I was supervising, we had people who would “forget” to copy someone on an email because they didn’t want that person involved. They’d say it was an accident, but after the third or fourth time, you knew. This is like that. They’re keeping things from me so I’ll stop being part of decisions about my sister.
Do you ever feel that things in your environment, like TV shows, news, or conversations, are sending you hidden messages or referring to you in some way?

Not so much the TV or the news, no… I mean, I don’t sit there thinking a commercial is about me or anything like that.

It’s more the real things around me, the things that keep happening. My sister’s appointments get moved, and somehow I’m the last to know. Bills come in wrong. People say they’ll call me back and then they just don’t. And everyone wants to say, “Oh, that’s just how offices are,” but I worked in an office for years, I supervised people, I know what normal mistakes look like. We had stacks of forms go missing once because someone put them behind the printer—ridiculous, but that was a mistake.

This feels different. It keeps coming back to the same point: I’m left out, I don’t get the information, and then when I ask questions I’m treated like I’m causing trouble. So no, not hidden messages from the television exactly. But I do feel like the pattern is telling me something—that they’re keeping information from me and trying to push me out of decisions about my sister.
Have you ever felt that certain events, objects, or actions in your life had a special or hidden meaning that others didn’t seem to understand?

I wouldn’t say objects, really… not like a vase means something or the TV is talking to me. It’s more events, the way things line up.

Like, my sister’s appointments get moved, and I’m not told until after, or I hear it from the wrong person. Then a bill shows up wrong, and then someone “forgets” to call me back. And everybody says, “That’s just a mistake,” but after months of it, it starts to mean something. It means I’m being kept out.

I used to supervise an office, and you could tell when things were just sloppy versus when people were quietly making sure someone didn’t get copied in. People think that’s paranoia, but offices have ways of doing that. So yes, I do think these things have a meaning other people don’t want to see—or don’t want to admit. The meaning is they’re trying to push me out of decisions about my sister.

patient.answer:
I wouldn’t say objects, really… not like a vase means something or the TV is talking to me. It’s more events, the way things line up.

Like, my sister’s appointments get moved, and I’m not told until after, or I hear it from the wrong person. Then a bill shows up wrong, and then someone “forgets” to call me back. And everybody says, “That’s just a mistake,” but after months of it, it starts to mean something. It means I’m being kept out.

I used to supervise an office, and you could tell when things were just sloppy versus when people were quietly making sure someone didn’t get copied in. People think that’s paranoia, but offices have ways of doing that. So yes, I do think these things have a meaning other people don’t want to see—or don’t want to admit. The meaning is they’re trying to push me out of decisions about my sister.

inference.note: The patient's beliefs align most closely with Delusional Disorder, as they demonstrate non-bizarre delusions focused on a specific theme (being excluded from decisions and information being withheld) without other prominent psychotic symptoms or functional decline seen in Schizophrenia or Schizoaffective Disorder.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits a persistent and unfounded belief that others are deliberately withholding information and attempting to exclude them from decisions regarding their sister, despite lack of external confirmation. The delusional ideation is non-bizarre, persistent, and circumscribed around this single theme, without broader disorganization, hallucinations, or mood symptoms.
